text:
maria-support: Heads up — we're getting a customer-facing p95/p99 regression for tenant acme starting ~09:15 UTC. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~850ms, p99 > 4s. Customers reporting timeouts & slow responses. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/ingress/ingress-latency?var-tenant=acme :warning:

arjun-oncall: Which region/shard? any recent deploys?

maria-support: ap-southeast-1 / shard-7. deploy-bot shows a DB migration finished at 09:10 by liam-eng. Attaching sample request ids: req_0a1b2c3d, req_0f9e8d7c.

liam-eng: I pushed a small auth-db index change this morning — could be related. Can you paste a couple of slow request logs?

maria-support: paste logs snippet:
```
[09:16:12] req=req_0a1b2c3d ingress: accept -> queue (queue_ms=420)
auth-service: start validate_token (trace=tx123)
auth-db: query SELECT user_id FROM tokens WHERE token=$1 (duration=2100ms)
auth-service: validate_token done (duration=2150ms)
model-proxy: start inference (wait_ms=50)
response sent (total=2450ms)
```

beth-cs: Customers on support at 09:20 saying multiple retries, some got 502s. SLA hit. Any quick mitigation?

arjun-oncall: If auth-db is the culprit, we can short-circuit validation with token-cache fallback for affected shard/tenant and bump admission-control limits for acme temporarily. Two steps: 1) enable auth-cache fallback, 2) increase inflight for tenant to avoid pileup (careful with downstream).

liam-eng: Confirmed — telemetry shows auth-db p99 for read latency spiked to ~2.2s across replica set right after the migration. Likely missing index or long-running compactions. I'm starting a rollback of the migration on replicas. Meanwhile we should enable the cache fallback.

maria-support: Repro steps I used for support ticket (minimal):
1) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"short prompt"}' -H 'x-tenant-id: acme'
2) observe 5-10 requests and check `ingress.latency.p99{tenant:acme}`
3) check ingress logs for req ids above and trace into auth-service

liam-eng: To enable fallback quickly (runbook):
```
# toggle per-shard auth cache fallback
redwood-cli feature-toggle set auth.cache_fallback true --shard shard-7
# increase tenant inflight cap
redwood-cli tenant-config set acme.max_inflight 80
```
I'll watch auth-db rollback/repair.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: successful rollback job triggered for migration-2026-03-17 on replicas shard-7 by liam-eng at 09:25 UTC.

arjun-oncall: Good. Also add short-term rate-limit for background-bulk operations from acme to reduce noisy fanout: `tenant.acme.rate_limit.background=10r/s`

beth-cs: I'll update the customer: "We identified a DB migration causing auth lookups to slow. We rolled back that change and enabled a cache fallback; you may see improved latency in the next ~5-10 minutes. We're monitoring and will follow up." :white_check_mark:

liam-eng: Rolled back migration on replicas and restarted auth-service pool. Observability now shows auth-db p95 down to ~80ms, p99 ~200ms. Ingress p95 back to ~140ms, p99 ~420ms and trending down.

maria-support: Confirming reduced error counts for acme. Will keep ticket open until 24h stable.

arjun-oncall: Followups: 1) add a health check alert for auth-db read latency > 500ms, 2) add pre-migration smoke test for token lookup perf, 3) add optional canary for DB index changes. I'll create tickets.

maria-support: Thanks all. Notes saved to ticket #SUP-4812 with repro steps and mitigation timeline.

liam-eng: Quick postmortem note: root cause was an unintended full-table scan introduced by migration on token table; fixed by rollback and adding index migration verification.

maria-support: Closing thread once we see 1 hour of stable p99 < 500ms for acme.

ops-bot: monitoring: uptime check for shard-7 auth latency OK as of 09:34 UTC.
